entries.result: Lemma 4.2, constants of the buffered discount
entries.title: Constants of the buffered discount
entries.summary: The argument of the note stands; the formal proof uses slightly different absolute constants, and the area-law constant stays linear in 1 + J/Δ.
entries.context: Lemma 4.2 surrounds an interval X by m nested shells of width R and shows that, conditioned on these shells, X keeps at most half of its entropy plus a constant. This constant and m enter the entropy bound of Theorem A.
entries.claims: The note fixes an energy constant CE = 8NRJq2(R+1), where NR bounds the number of terms crossing a cut, takes m as the least integer above four quantities, and bounds the energy of the reweighted state by Δ/4, so that the conditional entropy is at most ½S(X) + ½ + CE/Δ.
entries.found: The finite-dimensional estimate used in the formalization bounds the energy by twice the printed amount, so the argument runs with the energy bound Δ/2. The losses from the overlap with the ground state then sum to m log 2 instead of 2CE/Δ, and an error term of order (J/Δ)BR/m is kept explicitly instead of being absorbed by a fourth condition on m, which is dropped. The structure of the argument and its hypotheses are those of the note.
entries.impact: No. Only absolute constants change, the formal constants are explicit, and Theorem A holds with a constant C0(q, R)(1 + J/Δ) as stated.
entries.plan: Either revise the note to the formal constants, or prove the finite-dimensional discount with the sharper energy coefficient and restore the printed constants. Neither is needed for any later step.

entries.result: Proposition 7.1, sequential truncation in threshold form
entries.title: Sequential truncation by an eigenvalue threshold
entries.summary: Theorem B is proved as stated; the truncation lemma behind it is formalized in the form its proof uses, which differs from the printed form.
entries.context: Proposition 7.1 builds a matrix product state from a vector on the chain by projecting, at each cut, the left part onto a few eigenvectors of its reduced density matrix. The proof of Theorem B applies it with the eigenvalue bounds of the marginal tail bound.
entries.claims: For every bond dimension D, keeping the D largest eigenvalues at every cut gives a matrix product state of bond dimension at most D whose distance from the vector is at most the sum over the cuts of the square roots of the discarded weights.
entries.found: The formal lemma keeps, at each cut, the eigenvalues at least exp(−(Sk + w)), where Sk is the entropy of the left part and w a common slack. It proves that at most exp(Sk + w) eigenvalues are kept and bounds the error by the tail weights beyond w. The bond dimension is then an output of the lemma instead of a free parameter, so the printed statement for an arbitrary D is not formalized.
entries.impact: No. The proof of Theorem B in the note uses exactly the threshold form, and Theorem B is formalized without extra hypotheses.
entries.plan: Either formalize the printed proposition with the projection onto the D largest eigenvalues, reusing the existing product of projections and its error and rank bounds, or restate the proposition in threshold form.

entries.result: Theorem A, finite subsets of the integers
entries.title: Domains with gaps in the one-dimensional area law
entries.summary: Theorem A is formalized for every finite set of integers, as the note states it, with the constant of the chain.
entries.context: Theorem A allows any finite set Λ of integers, which may consist of several separated intervals, with edges between consecutive integers in Λ. Its proof first reduces to a single interval of consecutive sites.
entries.claims: The note reduces to one interval by writing the Hamiltonian as a sum over the separated pieces of Λ, factoring the gapped ground state as a product over the pieces, and adding entropies and boundaries over the pieces.
entries.found: The formal proof first treated only a chain of consecutive sites. It now covers every finite Λ by a shorter argument: across a gap of Λ the part to the left has zero entropy, and replacing a region by its symmetric difference with that part changes neither its entropy nor its boundary edges in Λ, so the chain theorem applies without factoring the ground state.
entries.impact: No. The theorem is proved with the hypotheses of the note.
